name: Ossivite-LX
description: A ceramic-titanium composite infused with osteogenic progenitor cells and BioForge's proprietary mineral-seeding matrix, Ossivite-LX is engineered to bond permanently with host skeletal tissue and grow into it over 6-12 weeks post-implantation. The ceramic lattice mimics trabecular bone architecture at the nanoscale, allowing natural vasculature to penetrate and remodel the material boundary. Over time, the distinction between implant edge and host bone becomes radiologically indistinguishable.
cost: Φ4,200 per kg (implant-grade billets); Φ800–Φ2,400 per pre-formed implant unit
story_hooks: A Tier 1 patient receives a black-market Ossivite-LX implant from a street fabricator using an uncertified mineral matrix — it bonds, but the vascular ingrowth is wrong, and the limb is slowly stiffening as the material over-mineralizes.

A forensic investigator discovers that a murder victim's Ossivite-LX implants have continued remodeling post-mortem, fed by residual cellular activity, subtly altering the evidence of blunt force trauma.

BioForge's latest batch of Ossivite-LX contains an undisclosed genetic marker that allows the corporation to claim partial biological ownership of anyone implanted with it under a controversial 2198 biopatent ruling.
